articles.title: New Play Area Under Construction in Alkrington, Middleton
articles.excerpt: Rochdale Council has commenced work on a new play area in Alkrington, Middleton, alongside improvements to two existing sites, enhancing recreational facilities for local families.
articles.content_html:
Rochdale Council has begun construction on a new play area named Mainway Meadows, located between Mainway and Moss Way in Alkrington, Middleton. The project aims to create a safe and inclusive space for children of various ages and abilities, featuring accessible pathways, safety fencing, and a range of play equipment including swings, a slide, seesaw, roundabout, seating, and a children’s picnic table.

The construction of Mainway Meadows is expected to take approximately four to five weeks. This initiative is funded by Middleton Township, with the council expressing gratitude for the support that will provide much-needed play facilities for local families.

In addition to the new play area, improvements are nearing completion at the Sandy Park play area in Alkrington. Councillor Dylan Williams noted the investment in new play equipment for Kirkway Stocks Play Park, also known as Farmway or Sandy Park, which is set to enhance recreational options for residents.

These developments reflect Rochdale Council's commitment to improving community facilities and ensuring that children have access to safe and enjoyable play environments. Local families can look forward to the completion of these projects in the coming weeks.

articles.title: Rochdale Boroughwide Housing Proposes Demolition of Seven Blocks in Lower Falinge
articles.excerpt: Rochdale Boroughwide Housing plans to demolish seven blocks of flats in Lower Falinge to make way for 270 new homes and improved public spaces as part of a long-term regeneration initiative.
articles.content_html:
Rochdale Boroughwide Housing (RBH) has unveiled plans to demolish seven blocks of flats in the Lower Falinge estate, aiming to construct 270 new homes. The targeted blocks, known as Ollerton, Newstead, Romsey, Quinton, Ullesthorpe, Zeburgh, and Vaynor, are deemed no longer fit for purpose after decades of use.

Located between St Mary’s Gate and Sheriff Street, the Lower Falinge estate has been undergoing regeneration for over a decade. This latest phase follows previous demolitions of the Waverley, Exbury, Yarwell, and Abbeydale blocks, which have already altered the landscape of the area. Although the new development is expected to provide a net gain of 150 homes, the overall housing stock in Lower Falinge will not increase due to these earlier demolitions.

In addition to the new housing, RBH plans to enhance public spaces and improve connectivity to Rochdale town centre through the introduction of cycle lanes and footpaths. The new homes will primarily be built on the land currently occupied by the blocks set for demolition, with additional plots on adjacent land also earmarked for development.

Before submitting an official planning application to Rochdale Council, RBH has prepared an Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) to address potential environmental and social impacts of the proposed development. This assessment will consider factors such as noise, dust from demolition, construction traffic, and pollution risks. Hannah Fleming, RBH's director of regeneration and asset improvement, expressed a commitment to creating a safe and affordable community in Lower Falinge, reflecting on the feedback received during recent consultations.

BREAKING NEWS — LIVE

A 13-year-old boy was seriously injured in a stabbing incident at a Taco Bell in Rochdale on Saturday evening, leading to the arrest of two teenage boys.

A 13-year-old boy has been seriously injured following a stabbing at a Taco Bell restaurant on Riverside Walk in Rochdale town centre. The incident occurred shortly after 6pm on Saturday, August 29, 2026, prompting a swift response from emergency services, including an air ambulance.

Greater Manchester Police (GMP) confirmed that the boy was taken to hospital with serious injuries. In connection with the incident, two teenage boys have been arrested on suspicion of assault and possession of a bladed article. Police have cordoned off the area around the restaurant as investigations continue.

Crime Scene Investigation officers were seen conducting enquiries at the scene, where a significant police presence was noted. Pictures from the location show officers outside the Taco Bell, which is understood to have been the site of the stabbing.

A spokesperson for GMP stated, "We were called to reports of a stabbing at 6.09pm on Riverside Walk. Enquiries are ongoing." The police have not released further details regarding the condition of the injured boy or the identities of the arrested teenagers.

The Greater Manchester Police’s Economic and Cyber Crime Unit is organising a series of drop-in events across Rochdale to help residents stay safe online. These events aim to raise awareness about the various forms of cyber crime, which can have serious consequences for victims, including financial loss and identity theft.

According to GMP, cyber crime encompasses a wide range of fraudulent activities, from identity theft and online transaction scams to dating fraud. The police highlighted that millions of cases of fraud and computer misuse are reported annually, many of which could be avoided by adopting better online habits.

Residents are encouraged to attend these events to learn practical steps to protect themselves from becoming victims of cyber crime. Simple measures, such as not sharing passwords or personal information and creating strong, unique passwords, can significantly reduce the risk of falling prey to online scams.

Details of the specific locations and times for the drop-in events have not yet been released, but residents should monitor local announcements for updates. This initiative reflects GMP's commitment to enhancing community safety in the digital age.

articles.title: Restoration of Historic Packer Spout Steps Completed in Rochdale Town Centre
articles.excerpt: The restoration of the Packer Spout steps, over 400 years old, has been completed, linking Rochdale Town Hall to St Chad’s Church, enhancing the town's historic landscape.
articles.content_html:
The restoration of the Packer Spout steps, a unique set of historic steps over 400 years old, has been completed in Rochdale town centre. These steps, which run through the Broadfield Park Slopes, connect the major historic attractions of Rochdale Town Hall and St Chad’s Church, the oldest church in the borough, which has parts dating back to Saxon times.

Dating from before 1660, the steps have a rich history, believed to have been used by mourning relatives who would ascend to St Chad’s Church to scatter rue and rosemary in the churchyard as offerings for their loved ones. The steps are situated in the recently restored Broadfield Park Slopes area, which during the Victorian period was known for its notorious slum, referred to as 'the gank'. This area was characterised by tightly packed housing, narrow passageways, and high crime rates, with many residents working in Rochdale’s mills.

The restoration project was undertaken by Oldham contractor Maysand, who faced significant challenges due to the steepness of the site. A special pulley system with tracks and rollers was devised to transport the stone up the hill. The team meticulously removed all 122 steps, many of which were broken and uneven, before reconstructing the area underneath and the damaged steps using traditional sandstone to match the existing stone.

The completion of this restoration not only preserves a significant piece of Rochdale's history but also enhances the town's landscape, making it more accessible for residents and visitors alike. The steps are expected to attract more foot traffic between the town hall and St Chad’s Church, contributing to the local heritage tourism.
